talking_points.headline: World Wealth Report 2026 crowns the orchestrator-banker — and benchmarks the AI bar Adam's pilots must clear
talking_points.context_html: Capgemini's World Wealth Report 2026 reframes the RM as an orchestrator of expertise, with Charles Boulton, CEO of Private Bank, HSBC UK among the voices quoted and Standard Chartered's GenAI-assisted MyWealth platform held up as the delivery template; it benchmarks JPMorgan at 400+ AI use cases and Morgan Stanley's OpenAI partnership. It lands the same week as HSBC's UK advice-desk cuts and Goldman Sachs' largest-ever advisor class — the industry is splitting, not converging, on the human-versus-machine advice model. For Adam, the report hands him a vendor-neutral yardstick for the AI-coach and portfolio-agent go/no-go calls due this quarter: the question is no longer whether AI augments advice, but which workflow it plugs into.

talking_points.headline: Agentic AI hits the org chart: index data shows peers industrialising agents while McKinsey puts $75bn of payments revenue at stake
talking_points.context_html: Evident's 2026 AI Index shows the front-runners moving from pilots to platforms: Citi's new group head of AI David Griffiths has rolled out Arc to deploy agentic tools bank-wide, Tan Su Shan, CEO of DBS describes agents across personal, team and enterprise lenses, and Héctor Grisi, CEO of Santander calls AI an operating-model redesign rather than a cost-cutting programme. In parallel McKinsey estimates agentic AI puts US$75 billion of payments revenue at risk by 2030 even as it creates US$110 billion of productivity upside. For Adam the two data points together mark the shift his portfolio must design for: agents are becoming production infrastructure with revenue and workforce consequences, and the controls plus capacity plans built this year decide whether his programmes ride that or react to it.

talking_points.headline: CMB Monaco goes live on the integrated Avaloq–Aladdin stack — the converged platform HSBC runs both halves of gets its first production reference
talking_points.context_html: CMB Monaco has become the first bank live on the integrated Avaloq–BlackRock Aladdin Wealth platform, days after DBS extended its Avaloq alliance across Asia with a S$1tn AUM ambition we covered yesterday. HSBC has run Aladdin for six years and Avaloq as its core, so a competitor now operates the same converged stack end-to-end — the catch-up framing no longer applies, and differentiation moves to advisory workflow, adoption and delivery pace. For Adam this tightens the vendor-convergence story around his Avaloq 6.1 track: the ground his change portfolio is built to hold is exactly where the competitive battle now sits.

On Adam's Desk.title: CMB Monaco becomes first bank live on integrated Avaloq–BlackRock Aladdin Wealth platform
On Adam's Desk.summary: CMB Monaco has gone live as the first bank on the integrated Avaloq and BlackRock Aladdin Wealth platform, combining core banking, portfolio management and advisory on one stack. The go-live lands days after DBS extended its own Avaloq alliance across Asia, showing the vendor consolidating reference clients at speed. For Adam, a competitor now runs the exact converged Avaloq-plus-Aladdin stack HSBC operates both halves of — so the differentiation question shifts squarely to advisory workflow and delivery pace, the terrain his 6.1 programme owns.

On Adam's Desk.title: Agentic AI threatens $75b of bank payments revenue by 2030, McKinsey warns
On Adam's Desk.summary: McKinsey estimates agentic AI could put US$75 billion of global payments revenue at risk by 2030 — with a further US$65 billion of deposit net interest income exposed — even as it creates up to US$110 billion in annual productivity upside for providers that adapt. The projection lands as Visa reports 63% of merchants already exploring agent-initiated payments. For Adam, machine-initiated payment flows collide directly with the payments-control work he is delivering; the end-of-cycle controls now being built must anticipate instructions initiated by software, not just by humans.

AI & Technology.title: Inside the 2026 AI Index: Citi's Arc platform industrialises agentic AI across the bank
AI & Technology.summary: Evident's 2026 AI Index profiles the banks turning AI into industrial capability: Citi's new group head of AI David Griffiths has rolled out Arc, a platform deploying agentic tools bank-wide, while DBS and Santander are cited for agentic and operating-model scale. Tan Su Shan, CEO of DBS, frames agents across personal, team and enterprise lenses, and Héctor Grisi, CEO of Santander describes AI as operating-model redesign rather than cost-cutting. For Adam the index is an external scorecard for the AI enablement inside his own portfolio — peers are industrialising agents, not piloting them.

Competitor Intelligence.title: Goldman Sachs hires more wealth advisors because AI is making clients harder to impress
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Goldman Sachs is running its largest-ever private wealth advisor training class — more than 120 advisors through a four-week boot camp this summer — explicitly because AI is making clients harder to impress and human advice more valuable at the top end. The move is a direct counter-narrative to the advice-desk cuts sweeping the industry. For Adam it sharpens the strategic question inside his own transformation: automate the bottom of the advice pyramid, premium humans at the top — and design the workflow that decides where each client lands.

Competitor Intelligence.title: Standard Chartered to offer digital asset custody to Singapore institutional clients
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Standard Chartered plans to launch institutional digital-asset custody in Singapore by end-2026, covering selected cryptocurrencies, stablecoins and tokenised real-world assets for institutional and accredited corporate clients, pending regulatory clearance. Ying Ying Tan, Global Head of Digital Assets at Standard Chartered, said the service will sit alongside the bank's existing financing and securities services in Singapore. For Adam, a key competitor is quietly completing a UAE–Luxembourg–Hong Kong–Singapore custody corridor while tokenisation stays on his programme's watchlist.

Competitor Intelligence.title: Standard Chartered rebrands GBS to Global Capability Centres across 21,000 staff
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Standard Chartered is retiring the Global Business Services name and rebranding its hubs as Global Capability Centres, reflecting broader technology and enterprise-capability roles across 21,000 staff in China, India, Malaysia, Poland and the Philippines, announced 7 October. The rebrand signals the global-bank centre model shifting from cost arbitrage to capability delivery. For Adam, whose own delivery model leans on Asia transformation centres, StanChart's framing is a live reference point in the ways-of-working debate his organisation review is circling.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: World Wealth Report 2026: the banker becomes an orchestrator of expertise
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: Capgemini's World Wealth Report 2026 argues the banker is becoming an orchestrator of expertise rather than a solo adviser, spotlighting Standard Chartered's MyWealth platform — RM portfolio proposals, ongoing reviews and GenAI-drafted client communications in one compliant workflow — and quoting Charles Boulton, CEO of Private Bank, HSBC UK on orchestrating the right expertise at the right moment. It benchmarks JPMorgan at 400+ AI use cases and Morgan Stanley's OpenAI partnership. For Adam the report is external validation of the advisory-workflow-first thesis behind his platform roadmap — and a vendor-neutral yardstick for his AI-coach and portfolio-agent pilots.
